column1: # Metabolites this repository INSTALLS into a host GEM, and what they are.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `data/thermo/aliases.tsv` is a vendored ModelSEED table: it maps
# ModelSEED compound ids onto ids from PUBLISHED models (AlgaGEM, BiGG, AraCyc, KEGG). A
# metabolite id that this repository invents when it installs a heterologous pathway --
# `phytoene_c`, from `src/ystwin/fba/carotenoid.py` -- is in no alias table anywhere and
# never will be, so `ThermodynamicData.load().dgf()` returned None for all three C40
# carotenoids. That was read as a coverage gap and written into
# `data/pathways/beta_carotene.toml` as "the vendored tables carry no formation energy for
# a C40 carotenoid". It was a NAMING gap: the tables carry all three.
# `docs/research/CAROTENOID_ENERGIES.md` is the corrected record.
# This file closes it as declared data. Each row states which species a repository-local
# metabolite id IS, by ModelSEED and KEGG identifier, with the source that establishes it.
# It is read by `src/ystwin/bridge/thermodynamic.py`.
# IT IS AUTHORED HERE, NOT DOWNLOADED, and `thermodynamic.py` therefore resolves it against
# the repository rather than through YSTWIN_THERMO -- a machine pointing that variable at
# its own copy of the ModelSEED download must still get these declarations.
# `formula` is checked against the ModelSEED entry on load, the same `_same_skeleton` check
# that already stops an alias resolving ribose-5-phosphate onto a chlorinated herbicide. A
# row whose formula disagrees with the database is refused rather than used.
# DECLARING AN ID IS NOT ENDORSING THE NUMBER BEHIND IT. See refuted_energies.tsv: all
# three rows below are also declared there, so the gate reports them as `cannot_say` for a
# stated reason rather than reporting a verdict off an extrapolated energy.
metabolite_id
phytoene_c
